Uniform Title: Kālīkalpalatā Secondary Title: Dakṣiṇakālīkalpalatā Author: Vimarśānandanātha
Manuscript: NGMCP 5-6521; Reel Number: B 120/9

Description: The *Kālīkalpalatā*, also known as the *Dakṣiṇakālīkalpalatā* by Vimarśānandanātha, concerns the ritual procedures for the worship of the goddess Dakṣiṇakālī and her consort Mahākāla. This form of Kālī is particularly popular in Bengal. First presented by Āgamakṛṣṇavāgīśa in his *Bṛhattantrasāra*—composed in Bengal during the sixteenth century—the *Kālīkalpalatā* is a later work. The ritual procedure is described in sufficient detail to enable its performance. It is divided into two sections (*kusuma*, literally "flowers"): the first deals with the preliminary purifications, bathing, and the offering of libations; the second describes the *pūjā* itself.
Notes: Revision 0: December 17, 2013 Publication Country: India 1a)
Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Salutations to the venerable Gurus.
Having bowed to the auspicious Kālī, who is the very essence of creation, preservation, and dissolution,
I shall indeed describe her ritual worship according to the prescribed tradition.

Having risen from the *brahmī-mudrā*, one who is well-seated in the lotus posture (*padmāsana*) should bow the head to the family tree (*kulavṛkṣa*) and meditate upon one's own guru, who resides within the lunar disc situated in the center of the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus at the crown of the head. As follows:
Red in color, with red unguents, garlands, and garments, holding a red lotus in his hand at night,

embraced by his beloved with intense passion, his face serene, bestowing the gestures of fearlessness and boons with both hands— he whose eyes are filled with the nectar of bliss beholds that supreme form of Śambhu.
One should meditate on the Guru seated upon one's head. Having thus meditated and worshipped with mental offerings, [one recites]:
*aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hare saphraṃ haskṣmaṃ lvryūṃ śkhphreṃ śkṣma lkṣmīṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ śrī-amukānandanātha śrī amuka-devy-āṃ vā*.
I worship the auspicious sandals.
Having thus recited the mantra of the Guru’s sandals ten or seven times, [one should say]:
"O Śrī Guru, you who are the protector of the most secret of secrets, accept this recitation performed by us; O Maheśvara, by your grace, may there be success for me, O Lord."
Having offered [the gift], one should prostrate on the ground like a staff. The mantra for prostration is as follows:
"Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state was revealed—the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and the non-moving are pervaded."
Thus, having prostrated, let there be salutation to you, O Lord, the Blessed One, Śiva in the form of the Guru,
who assumes manifold forms according to his own will for the sake of accomplishing the descent of music.
And for that which is devoid of the manifestation of difference through all cognitions— being non-dual, formless, and of a single nature in the ultimate sense— there is no such thing.
Salutations to the Self who is Śiva, whose form is fashioned from independent compassion;
who is dependent upon others for his devotees, yet possesses a beautiful form for those destined for liberation.
For the sake of discernment for those who have already discerned, for the sake of investigation for those who investigate,
for the sake of illumination for those who are luminous, and for the sake of the nature of knowledge for those who possess knowledge.
I shall offer salutations in front, on both sides, behind, and above; O Creator, please prepare a new seat for me, who am ever present in the form of the mind.

Having thus praised and bowed, and having received his command, [one should meditate upon] that which resides in the *mūlādhāra*, within a triangle, deep-seated, with its opening encircling the *śivaliṅga*, coiled like a sleeping serpent, possessing three folds in the form of a conch-spiral, and radiant with the luster of ten million flashes of lightning— [like] a grain of wild rice.
Having made the primordial nature (prakṛti), which possesses a body like a thorn and consists of the elements, conscious by means of the seed-syllable of fire in the triangle,
and having led it through the channel of Suṣumṇā up to the end of the twelve [fingers] into the aperture of Brahmā (brahmaraṃdhra);

[The practitioner] should contemplate his own Guru right there within that [light], which is the seat of the thousand-petaled lotus situated at the crown of the head, united with Śiva, and being satiated by the stream of nectar trickling down from the lunar disc located there. As it is said:
With hearts submerged in the nectar-essence of the Kula, with eyes powdered [by that vision],
and with the darkness of ignorance pulverized by the embrace of the Kula;
for those surrounded by Kula-disciples, their bodies are filled with fullness.
2a) From the entire [mantra] endowed with the gestures of boon-granting and fearlessness, which fulfills all desires according to its family.
Having meditated thus.
Oṃ, salutation to Prahlādānandanātha; salutation to Sakalānandanātha.
Salutation to Kumārānandanātha. Salutation to Vasiṣṭhānandanātha.
Salutation to Krodhānandanātha. Salutation to Sundarānandanātha.
Salutation to Dhyānānandanātha. Salutation to Bodhānandanātha. Salutation to Sukānandana.

Having thus reflected, "Namas," one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) of the seers (*ṛṣi*) and so forth, preceded by the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) placement. Then, having brought Kuṇḍalinī from the twelve-petaled heart-lotus into the form of the Goddess according to the method to be described:

Having meditated upon her, one should worship with mental offerings of fragrance and the like. One should recite the Gāyatrī mantra twenty-eight times: "We know Kālī of the south; we meditate upon Hrūṃ Vāṃ Muḍā and the others; may she impel us. Then, having chanted the root mantra one hundred times, [one should proceed].
O Protectress of the most secret of secrets, accept this recitation performed by us;
O Great Goddess, may success be mine through your grace.

Having offered [the oblation] with this mantra using the left hand, one should request the command (*ājñā*) of the Goddess: "O Mother of the Universe, O Triśakti, even though you are the consciousness of the three worlds, by your command alone shall I rise at dawn and follow the course of my daily life for the sake of your pleasure. Having thus prayed, the Kuṇḍalinī should again be restored to her original state.
Having brought [the consciousness] to the *mūlādhāra*, one should contemplate its identity with that.
2b) Then,

[he beheld] that woman whose nature is bliss, who was manifesting in his hearing during the first departure and who remained as if immortal even during the return; therefore, she followed along the path step by step.
"I take refuge. Thus ends the meditations on Kuṇḍalinī.
"I am the Goddess and none other; I am Brahman itself, not subject to sorrow.
One should contemplate the Great Self as being of the nature of existence, consciousness, and bliss.
Thus, having explained the identity of the Guru, the Goddess, and the Self:
"O Goddess Mekhalā, who dwells upon the ocean and whose breasts are the mountain ranges!
O Consort of Viṣṇu, salutations to you; forgive my touch of your feet."

Thus, following her breath, having placed her foot upon the ground, having performed the necessary rites toward the southwest, and having become pure, the Goddess went to her abode; there, having taken up the remains of the previous offerings (*nirmālya*), having prostrated and received permission, she departed for the sacred bathing place (*tīrtha*) to bathe.
Thus ends the morning duties.

This must indeed be performed as an obligatory duty (*āvaśyaka*), because it is heard in scripture that there is a transgression (*pratyavāya*) for its non-performance. As it is said in the *Rudrayāmala*:
"He who, having failed to perform the morning [rites], worships the Goddess with devotion..."
But his worship is fruitless, like a ritual performed without purity.
Now, regarding the ritual bath (*snāna*): Visualizing oneself as the Goddess, having gone to a sacred bathing place (*tīrtha*), one should apply clay to the body with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*).
Taking *kuśa* grass in the form of gold and silver coins, [one should perform] everything for the Goddess.
Having meditated on the form and recited the root mantra, one should perform the removal of impurities, bathe, and sip water;
then, having placed sesame seeds, unbroken rice, *jaya* grass, and flowers into a vessel filled with water, one should not make a formal ritual resolve (*saṃkalpa*).
"Oṃ, beginning with 'today' and so forth, for the pleasure of such-and-such deity, I shall perform the ritual placement of the mantra (maṃtrasthāpana).
Having thus made this formal resolve (saṃkalpa), one should draw a triangle in the water, [reciting]:
"O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, and Sarasvatī..."
O Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī, take up your residence in these waters.

Having invoked the sacred waters (*tīrtha*) with this mantra, [one should draw them] from the solar orb using the *alaṅkuśa* mudrā. Then, at the end of the root-mantra (*mūla-mantra*) or the root-seed-syllables (*mūla-bīja*), one should offer libations (*ārghya*) with: "To the *ātmatattva*, svāhā! To the *vidyātattva*, svāhā! To the *śivatattva*, svāhā!
Or else, having sipped water (*ācamana*) three times with "Oṃ hrīṃ svāhā," one should [offer it] to oneself.

Having sprinkled it three times with this [mantra], applied clay to the limbs, and closed the seven apertures such as the ears and so forth, one should immerse oneself three times while recollecting the root mantra; likewise, having performed *ācamana* (ritual sipping) three times with the root mantra, one should drink water from the crown of the head three times using the *kumārī-mudrā*. This is the *mantra-snāna*. Thus it is stated in the *Kumārī*:

"Tantra, Veda, Ādi, Ananta, as well as Māyā and Svāhā—this is remembered as the *āvarta*. Now, following the Vedic *saṃdhyā*, one should perform the ritual of the *mantra-saṃdhyā*. As it has been said:
"Having performed the threefold [rites] immediately after bathing according to the very procedure already stated..."
Having performed the Vedic and Tantric twilight rituals (saṃdhyā), one should perform the libation (tarpaṇa).
Then, the Tantric twilight ritual (*saṃdhyā*) is as follows: Then, having put on two garments, [one should perform the protection] with the mantra:
*amaṇi pariṇi vajriṇi mahāpratisare rakṣarakṣa huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. With this mantra, one should bind the topknot (*śikhābandha*), and with the root mantra (*mūla*), apply the sectarian mark (*tilaka*).

3b) Having consecrated whatever substance [is intended], one should apply a *tilaka* marked with the sign of the *śakti* on the forehead, at the root of the hair (*udvaya*), and at the heart; one should fashion the mark of the *śakti* according to the procedure prescribed in one's own ritual manual.

The animal substance (pāśava) is purified by means of *agnihotra* ash and the like; however, according to the *Virakalpa*, it is [purified] by cemetery ash (*citābhasma*) or by rubbing with that [ash]. Having sipped water (*ācamya*) by means of the "upward-facing" [mudrā] through the previously mentioned procedure, one should perform the placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) starting with the heart and so forth, using the *kṛmi* seed-syllable for the vital breaths (*prāṇāyāma*). Having done this with the left hand...

Taking up water (*nala*) with the right hand, covering it with the left, and reciting "Haṃ Paraṃ Laṃ Va" three times, one should touch the root of the thumb with the *tattvamudrā* and the drops produced by snapping the fingers; having sprinkled [the water] seven times upon the head, one should place the remaining water in the right hand and bring it near the nose.
Drawing in all sins existing within the body through the space between the nostrils, one should wash them away with that water,

which becomes black in color; then, having gathered that water through the right nostril into the hand while the eyes are closed, one should cast it onto the prepared vajra-stone with the mantra *oṃ kraḥ astrāya phaṭ*, and then offer three handfuls of water to the Sun with the root mantra.
Having offered [the oblation], one should recite the Gāyatrī mantra— *kālikā vai vigrahasmajñānavāsinyai dhīmahi | tanno ghore pracodayāt*—
one hundred and eight times, or twenty-eight times, or twelve times, or eight times; this is the procedure for the twilight rituals (*saṃdhyā*) here.
4a) Now, the libation (tarpaṇa).
First, having visualized there a lotus-seat with eight petals upon the water, [one should place] one [deity] in each of the eight directions.

And in the center, one should satisfy the powers of the nine seats (*navapīṭhaśakti*). As follows: "I satisfy *Iṣṭā* [at the end of *jñāna*], *Śaktiyā*, *Ikāminī*, *Kāmadā*, *Vinītā*, *Ravinandanapriyā*, *Ānandā*, and *Manonmīnī* by means of the ritual acts for the sake of desire. This is the satisfaction (*saṃtarpaṇa*). Then, on that seat, that which is about to be described—

O Goddess, having visualized [the deity] there, one should invoke the deity here with the mantra: "Oṃ, may the deity come here. Oṃ, may Brahmabhairava be satisfied. Oṃ, may Viṣṇubhairava be satisfied. Oṃ, may Rudrabhairava be satisfied.
Hasakṣamalavarayūṃ, vauṣaṭ to Ānandabhairava. May Ānandabhairava be satisfied.

*Hasakṣamalavarayī sudhādevyai vauṣaṭ*. From Ānandabhairavī. Thus is the libation for the deities (*devatarpaṇa*). Now, the libation for the sages (*ṛṣitarpaṇa*): *Oṃ mahādevyaṃ vāḷ oṃ mahādevanandanāthas tṛpyatu oṃ tripurāṃ vā tṛpyatu oṃ bhairavānandanāthas tṛpyatu*. Thus for the divine lineage (*divyaughā*). *Oṃ*.

Oṃ, may Vighnānandanātha be satisfied. Oṃ, may Pūrṇānandanātha be satisfied. Oṃ, may Balacittānandanātha be satisfied. Oṃ, may Calācalānandanātha be satisfied. Oṃ, may Kumārānandanātha be satisfied. Oṃ, may Krodhānandanātha be satisfied. Oṃ, may Varānandanātha be satisfied.
Oṃ, Smaradīpanānandanātha is the protector of the four directions.
Oṃ, Māpāvatya is the protector of the wind. These are the Siddhas. Oṃ.
Vimalānandanātha, svāhā. Oṃ Kuśalānandanātha, svāhā.
Oṃ Bhīmasenānandanātha, svāhā. Oṃ Sudhākarānandanātha, svāhā. Bhīmānandanātha, svāhā. Aṅgorakṣānandanātha, svāhā. Oṃ.

Bhojadevānaṃdanātha, svāhā. Oṃ Prajāpatyānaṃdanātha, svāhā. Oṃ Samayānaṃdanātha, svāhā. Oṃ Saṃtoṣānaṃdanātha, svāhā. Thus ends the [offering to] the human lineage. Now, the libation to the ancestors (pitṛtarpaṇa): [to] the Gurus, Paramagurus, Parāparagurus, and Parameṣṭhīgurus, [and] Ānaṃdanātha.
One should satisfy the deities of sound. This libation (*tarpaṇa*), however, is performed when the Guru has departed for the next world; while he remains here, it is performed for only a moment.

Then, having meditated there upon the Goddess together with her retinue and having worshipped her with perfumes and other offerings, one recites ten times over the root mantra: "O Mother Kālikā, together with Mahākāla on the right, may you be satisfied."
Or, having satiated Mahākāla three times, one should satisfy the deities together with their retinues, as follows:

Āṃ, salutation to the heart; I satiate the deity of the heart. Krāṃ, svāhā to the head; [I satiate] the deity of the head. Kru, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock; I satiate the deity of the crest-lock. Krai, hūḥ to the armor; I satiate the deity of the armor. Krau, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes; I satiate the deity of the eyes. Kraḥ, phaṭ to the weapon.
Phaṭ! I satiate the Astra-deity.
(5a) "Svāhā" is used everywhere; "idaṃ" is the traditional teaching. Then, having recited the root mantra...

I satisfy Śrī Dakṣiṇakālikā, the deity of the first enclosure. Having thus satisfied the root goddess, then follows the satisfaction of the second enclosure: Oṃ Kālīntaḥ, Oṃ Kapālilīntaḥ, Oṃ Kullāta, Oṃ Kurukullānta, Oṃ Virodhinī Laṃḥ, Avipracittāntaḥ, Oṃ Umātāntaḥ, Oṃ Umaprabhāntaṃ.

Oṃ from Dīkṣā, Oṃ from Nīlānta, Oṃ from Ghanānta, Oṃ from Valākā, [Oṃ] from Mātrānta, Oṃ from Mudrānta, Oṃ from Minānta. Then, having recited the root mantra and offered libations with "I satiate Śrī Kālī who resides in the second enclosure," one performs the libation for the third enclosure: Oṃ Āṃ from Brāhmī, Oṃ Aḥ...
Having recited the *nārasimhīta* root mantra from that point, I satisfy Śrī Kālikā, who consists of the third enclosure (*tṛtīyāvaraṇa*).

Then follows the libation for the fourth enclosure: *aiṃ hrīṃ aṃ asitāṅgabhairavāya namaḥ*, *aiṃ hrīṃ i ruru-bhairavāya namaḥ*, *aiṃ hrīṃ u caṇḍabhairavāya namaḥ*, *aiṃ hrīṃ ṝ krodhabhairavāya namaḥ*. *Aiṃ...*
*Hrīṃ ḷ*, [I satisfy] Unmattabhairava; *Aiṃ hrīṃ ai*, [I satisfy] Ekapālabhairava; *Aiṃ hrīṃ auṃ*, [I satisfy] Bhīṣaṇabhairava;
*Aiṃ hrīṃ aḥ*, [I satisfy] Saṃhārabhairava. Having recited the root mantra for the libation (*tarpaṇa*), one says:
"I satisfy Śrī Kālikā, who consists of the fourth enclosure."

5b) Then, the libation for the five obstructions (*pañcāvaraṇa-tarpaṇa*): Oṃ i iṃ [to] Agni; na ma ya maṃ ta kṣa [to] Nairṛti; ta vaṃ [to] Varuṇa; tta yaṃ [to] Vāyu; ta śaṃ [to] Soma; ta haṃ [to] Īśāna; ta hrīṃ.
From the end [of the mantra], having uttered *oṃ* and the root-mantra of Brahmā, one should say: "I satiate Śrī Kālikā, who consists of the fifth enclosure (*pañcamāvaraṇa*).
Then, for the sixth enclosure, the satiation is as follows: from the end of *vaṃ*, *śaṃ*; from the end of *śakti*, *idaṃ*; [and] "I satiate Daṇḍa."

*Khaṃ* [to] the sword, *paṃ* [to] the noose, *śaṃ* [to] the goad, I offer libation; *gaṃ* [to] the mace, *triṃ* [to] the trident, *caṃ* [to] the discus, *paṃ* [to] the lotus—having uttered the root mantra, I offer libation to Śrī Kālikā, who consists of the sixfold enclosure. Then: *Oṃ* [to] the sword, *oṃ* [to] the mace, *oṃ* [to] the boon-granting gesture... *oṃ*.

"Abhayanta" is the supreme libation (*tarpaṇa*). Alternatively, having performed the libation for the Śaktis with the root mantra one hundred and eight times, or twenty-eight times, one performs the libation with the mantras of the six-limbed deities (*ṣaḍaṅgadevatā*). Then:
*hrīṃ hasaḥ mārta*. Oṃ, to Bhairava, together with the illuminating Śakti.

Having offered the *arghya* to the Sun three times with "This *arghya*, Svāhā," and having visualized the Goddess within the solar orb, one should offer it at the end of the root mantra with the formula: "To her who dwells in the rising orb of the Sun, who consists of the consciousness of Śiva, accompanied by Mahākāla—this *arghya*, Svāhā! while using a vessel filled with red sandalwood paste, hibiscus flowers, *kuśa* grass, unbroken rice, and water.

Having offered *arghya* with a copper vessel to the Goddess residing in the solar orb, and having recited the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) as many times as possible, one should offer it into the solar orb with the *guhya* mantra.

The Goddess, having gone to a body of water for a bath preceded by remembrance [of the deity], performed the bath that removes impurities; then, having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*) beginning with "Oṃ, today... and so forth, she visualized the water as the form of radiant energy identical with the Goddess, immersed herself three times while reciting the root mantra, sipped water again (*ācamana*), touched her crest-lock (*śikhā*) with the root mantra, and [performed the assignment of] the seer (*ṛṣi*) and other [limbs].

Having performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) and practiced breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), one should recite the root mantra or the Gāyatrī nine times in the morning, thirty-six times at midday, and sixteen times in the evening; thereafter, having offered the Vedic libations (*tarpaṇa*), one should meditate upon [the Goddess] together with Mahākāla, accompanied by her retinue, weapons, and serpents, along with all her limbs.

Having offered libations three times with "I satisfy Śrī Dakṣiṇakālikā, svāhā," and having presented the arghya to the Sun with the mantra "Oṃ Hrīṃ Haṃsaḥ," one should recite the root mantra as many times as possible, bid farewell to the Goddess, take holy water in a pure vessel, and proceed to the temple of the Goddess.
Thus ends the first flower in the *Dakṣiṇakālīkalpalatā*, composed by the venerable Vimarśānandanātha.

Now, the procedure for worship (*pūjāvidhi*). Therein, having put on two garments according to one's desire and having applied *tilaka* on the forehead, one approaches the vicinity of the worship chamber [reciting]: "The Sun, the Moon, Yama, Time, and the five great elements—these..."
O Goddess, you are the witness here to the new deeds, both auspicious and inauspicious; like a common painting, he is overcome by evil.
6b) "May it not be mine; may that evil be expelled from me, *phaṭ phaṭ*, homage to you!
Having thus performed the expulsion of evil with these two mantras, [one should proceed] with the mantra: *oṃ vajrarekhe huṃ phaṭ svāhā*.
Having brought water and sprinkled it over the worshiper, he should sit down.

Then, having washed his hands and feet with the mantra: *oṃ viśuddhasarvapāpāni śamayāśeṣavikalpān apanaya haṃ*, and with the mantra *oṃ hrīṃ svāhā*, he should bind his topknot (*śikhā*) if it has not already been bound.
Having performed the binding of the topknot (śikhābandhana) with the mantra, one should establish the general water offering (sāmānyārghya). As follows:

Having drawn a mandala consisting of a triangle, a circle, and a square, and having worshipped it with "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti," one should place the support (ādhāra). Then, having washed the vessel with "Oṃ astrāya phaṭ" and placed it upon the support, one should fill it with water while reciting "Oṃ krīṃ,
obeisance to the Heart," and invoke the previously mentioned sacred waters with "Oṃ."

One should not scatter perfumes and other offerings; rather, one should display the *dhenu-mudrā*. This is the general *arghya*. With that water, while sprinkling the four doors, one should worship the deities: "Oṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati" at the entrance; "obeisance to Kṣetrapāla" on the left; "obeisance to Vaṭuka" on the right; and "obeisance to the Yoginīs" at the base.
In this very order: homage to Gaṅgā, homage to Yamunā, homage to Śrī Lakṣmī, homage to Sarasvatī.

In this manner, one should worship the eastern and other doors. Then, one should address the door-keepers at the door: "Protect the door, warding off the multitude of wicked men"—this is the command of the Supreme Goddess. Having thus caused the divine command to be heard, one should exit from the pavilion while contracting the left limb.

"Oṃ rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. With the mantra "Oṃ sarvavighnānusāraya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā," one should perform the expulsion of obstacles by scattering consecrated *akṣata* rice. Then, having purified the ground with the mantra "Oṃ rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā," [one should recite] "Oṃ pavitra vajre hūṃ phaṭ svāhā."

Having consecrated the ground with the mantra "Āsurekhe vajrarekhe hūṃ phaṭ svāhā," one should draw a triangular maṇḍala there. Then, having worshipped it with the mantra "Oṃ hrīṃ ādhāraśaktaye namaḥ," and having worshipped the seat (āsana) therein, one should touch it with the hand while reciting the mantra "Pṛthvi tvayā... [from the Merupṛṣṭha].
Salutation to the Seer (ṛṣi); [place] on the head. Salutation to the meter (chandas), Sutala; [place] in the mouth. Salutation to the deity (devatā), Kūrma; [place] at the heart. 7b)

Having placed the palms of the hands together at the heart, this is the application (*viniyoga*) for sitting upon the seat. Thus, having remembered the seer (*ṛṣi*) and the other [limbs], and having touched [the seat] with the hand:
"O Goddess, the worlds are supported by you; you are supported by Viṣṇu; O Goddess, support me."
And purify the seat.
Having offered the seat with this mantra, one sits facing north upon the hero’s support (vīrādhāra).

At this juncture, O Hero, one should accept the *kuladravya* (substance of the lineage) which is divine in nature, but not that of the fettered (*pāśava*). Having bowed, saying "Guṃ, obeisance to the Gurus" on the left, "Gaṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati" on the right, and "Obeisance to Śrī Dakṣiṇakālikā" in the center, one should place the *argha* vessel on the left and set a small amount of water in the *prokṣaṇī* vessel; with that [water]...

Having sprinkled oneself with the collection of materials for worship, one should place flowers and other items on one's right side; behind that, a vessel for washing the hands; behind that, in the case of the Vīrakalpa, the family substances (kuladravya), or in the Pāśava system, pure water; and on the left, in another vessel, the food offerings (naivedya) and so forth.

With the mantra: "Oṃ, O Puṣpaka, you who are worthy of the king, born of the Lord; Oṃ, Puṣpe, Puṣpe, Mahāpuṣpe, Supuṣpe, O you who are born of flowers, and you who are strewn with flowers, svāhā!"—one should purify the flower.
Then, with the mantra "Hāṃ Huṃ Phaṭ" and the Nārāca-mudrā, one should gaze at it while reciting "samudra."

8a) Having performed the purification of all the requisites, such as incense and so forth, according to the ritual, and having purified body, speech, and mind by touching the tip of the lamp flame with the mantra *oṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*, [one recites] *rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ*.

Having placed the hand upon the heart with "phaṭ svāhā" and performed self-protection (*ātmarakṣā*), one should rub sandalwood-smeared flowers with both hands, take them in the left hand, and recite: "O Ācchāyā, may all those who wish me harm go to destruction; may death, disease, fear, and affliction strike that enemy upon his head. Thus.

Having cast three *tālas* (hand-claps) from afar in the northeastern direction with the root mantra alone, having purified the directions beginning with the east by joining the index finger and thumb, and having performed the directional binding (*digbandha*) both below and above,
one should contemplate the five-syllabled *kullukā* of Kālī— *krīṃ huṃ strīṃ hrīṃ phaṭ*— upon the crown of the head.
One should perform the installation of the Śakti. As it has been said:

"Then, having brought sixteen women who are proficient in mantras—the young, intoxicated with passion, well-dressed, smiling beautifully, always desirous of sexual union, and whose heads are marked by signs of accomplishment—for the sake of the practitioner..."

The wise man should place his own beloved, endowed with love, on his left side; having performed for her the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) and other rites, he should indeed perform the placement of the Mātṛkās.

8b) Having then performed breath control (prāṇāyāma), having caused it to be performed according to the rule, one should perform the installation of the Śakti; this is the procedure for the Divyavīraka [tantra]. In the Pāśakalpa, however, having gone to the door of the Goddess there...

Having filled a copper vessel with water and having placed fragrant scents and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) therein, one should consecrate it eight times with the *Tāra* mantra or with the seed-syllable (*bīja*). This is the general *arghya*.
Having sprinkled the door with that water and having worshipped the door according to the previously mentioned method, one should dispel the obstacles (*vighna*).

Contracting the limbs, entering within while leading with the right foot, one should worship and pay homage to the Vāstu deity in the southwest with "Oṃ Vāstudevatāyai namaḥ. Having worshipped the seat (śāsana) with the previously mentioned mantra, sitting facing north, one should perform the binding of the directions (digbandha) with the root mantra. [Then follows] Kullaka: *Suddhi* in the heart.

Regarding the bridge: for the sake of purification, one should perform the ritual rinsing of the mouth (*ācamana*) after contemplating the great bridge of the thousand-spoked wheel—the syllable *krīṃ* which will be described—located at the navel as *nirvāṇa*. For example: having rinsed the mouth three times with this syllable *krīṃ*, one should say: "Obeisance to Kālī; obeisance to Kapālinī."
Having wiped the two lips twice with the mantra "Oṃ kalpayai namaḥ," one should wash the hands with water and touch the seven apertures,
beginning with the heart,
as follows: "Oṃ kuru-kulāyai namaḥ."

9a) At the mouth: *namaḥ* to Virodhinī; *namaḥ* to Vipravittā. At the nose: *namaḥ* to Umā. At the eyes: *namaḥ* to Dīptā; *namaḥ* to Nīlā. At the ears: *namaḥ* to Dhanā. At the navel: *namaḥ* to Valākā.

*Namaḥ*. On the chest: *mātrāyai namaḥ*. On the head: *mudrāyai*. On the arms: *mitāyai*. Having thus performed the ritual sipping (*ācamana*), one should perform the binding of the directions (*digbandhana*) with the mantra *hūṃ ruḥ hrīṃ astrāya phaṭ*, and then perform breath control (*prāṇāyāma*). As follows:
Saying "namaḥ" at the *mūlādhāra*, and having joined [the hands] while holding the right nostril with the right thumb,
one should recite the *praṇava* or the root-mantra (*mūlamantra*) sixteen times while filling the air through the left nostril;
then, holding the left nostril with the little finger and the ring finger, one should [proceed] from the root [mantra]...

Having rotated [the mantra] sixty-four times and having drawn [the air] in through the left nostril, one should exhale the air through the right nostril with [the mantra] rotated thirty-two times; this is one [cycle]. Again, holding the left nostril with the little finger and the ring finger, [one should exhale] with [the mantra] recited sixteen times.
Having filled [the breath] through the right nostril, and then holding the right nostril with the thumb,
one should perform *kumbhaka* (retention) while reciting the root mantra sixty-four times; then, one should inhale through the left nostril while reciting it twenty-two times— this is another method.

9b) Again, having performed inhalation (*pūraka*) and retention (*kuṃbhaka*) with the previously mentioned *vāmanāsā* (left nostril) mudrā, one should exhale only the air through the right [nostril] for the duration of the previously stated number of measures (*mātrā*), beginning with the root [syllable].
In this regard, having performed three rounds of *prāṇāyāma*— namely, inhalation (*pūraka*) by means of the root mantra, retention (*kuṃbhaka*) with four [repetitions],
and exhalation (*recaka*) with two— one should then, on a seat consisting of the *nādi*,
use either *kuṇḍa*, *gola*, *svayaṃbhū*, *kusuma*, *kuṅkuma*, *agaru*, or *svayaṃbhū-kusuma-kuṇḍa-gola-hi-agorocanā*.

Having smeared the surface with one substance—either camphor, saffron, musk, wine, or sandalwood—one should, using a needle made of gold or other metal, draw a design consisting of five dots, a triangle, eight petals, and a single line within a four-continent square.
In the *Mṛtimāyā* [tantra], this belongs to the *Vīrakalpa*; however, in the *Pāśavakalpa*, it is as follows:

Having drawn [the design] upon objects endowed with jewels and the like, using either red sandalwood or plain sandalwood paste, one should carve it with a single [tool] and perform the consecration (*pratisthā*). That consecration is performed according to the prescribed measurements, whether the object is fashioned from gold or other metals, and so forth; it is then washed according to the ritual procedure prescribed in the Vedas.
Having performed the fire-transference (*agnyuttāraṇa*) rite, one should establish the cooked [offering] on the left side;
[this is done] on the tenth lunar day (*tithi*) and under the [corresponding] weekday (*vāra*).

At a distinguished moment on an auspicious day favorable to the querent, during a fixed *lagna*, when the moon is full and there is the rising of a favorable breath (*śubhaśvāsodaya*), [the result occurs] either upon the attainment of a desired object,
at the time of one's own birth, at the death of a teacher, or at the time of a conjunction (*yoga*) or after the performance of a ritual application (*prayoga*).

Having sprinkled [the object] separately with water from the coconut of moderate and small size, and with water that is a decoction of the medicinal herbs (varṇauṣadhi) for the letter *śva*, or with water that is a decoction of the medicinal herbs for the letters *karpūra* and *bīja*; [the medicinal herbs are as follows]: for the letter *i*, camphor;
for the *anusvāra*, *gorocanā*; for the letter *ka*, *pippala*; for the letter *ra*, *vitvakara*.
Having sprinkled [the deity] with water infused with medicinal herbs using these mantra-syllables, having washed [it] with fragrant water and barber’s water,

and having performed the worship up to the end of the pedestal-worship (*pīṭhapūjā*), one should place that *cakra* upon that pedestal; then, having invoked the Goddess into its center and visualized the attendants (*varaṇas*) each in their respective places, [one should worship] with the root-mantra consisting of the first peak-syllable (*kūṭa*).
Having worshipped three times as prescribed,
and having fully honored the Cakra, he should again worship it according to the stated sequence while reciting the clear root-mantra ten thousand times, offering incense and lamps.
Having likewise worshipped and paid obeisance to the Goddess, the Śaktis, and the Sāmavikas with various kinds of food and offerings,
one should dismiss them; however, for three days one should not dismiss the Goddess, [worshipping her] at the three junctions of the day every day.

One should perform the worship according to the method prescribed for the daily rite (*nityapūjā*). This same procedure applies even to the ritual diagrams (*prayogayantra*); on whichever day one performs either the entire rite or merely the consecration (*saṃskāra*), having done so exactly as ordained for that occasion, then on the fourth day, having diligently satisfied the Guru and with his permission, one should practice the daily sequence (*nityakrama*). Thus [ends the section on] the *cakra*.
For an image made of stone (*āmra*), consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*) must be performed again after twelve years;
for one made of silver, after twenty-two years; for one made of gold, for as long as one lives; and for those made of crystal and the like, as long as the lines [of the image] remain.
Having thus consecrated the yantra and placed a flower upon it, one should perform the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*). As follows:

By means of the syllable *huṃ*, one should raise the *kuṇḍalinī* from the *mūlādhāra*, unite the individual soul (*jīvātman*) with the Supreme Soul (*paramātman*) through the mantra *haṃsaḥ*, and dissolve [the former] into the latter. Then, one should dissolve the earth element situated from the feet up to the knees by means of the *tattva* of earth; the water element situated from there up to the navel by the *tattva* of water; and [finally] that which is situated from the navel up to the heart.
And that which is said to be carried upward is from the heart and so forth, ending at the midpoint of the eyebrows (bhrūmadhya).

Furthermore, the union (yauta) is from the midpoint of the eyebrows and so forth, situated within the ether (ākāśa) at the end of the Brahma-aperture (brahmarandhra), or [the letter] *taṃ* is in the ego-principle (ahaṃkāra).

Having dissolved that [ego] into the Great Principle (mahattattva), and that into primordial nature (prakṛti), and finally that into Brahman, one then visualizes the sin resembling a human being: beginningless with latent impressions (vāsanā) and consciousness, having the murder of a Brahmin for its head, the theft of gold for its two arms, the drinking of liquor for its two thighs, and violating the teacher’s bed for its two hips.
O limb, that pair of feet joined with it is a great sin;
its body-hairs are minor offenses, and its eyes are red with tears.
One should visualize the excellent sword and shield, the size of a thumb,

facing downwards and black in color, on the right side of the abdomen. Having thus visualized the personification of sin (pāpapuruṣa), one should recite the seed-syllable *yam* sixteen times through the left nostril.

Having filled it with air, one should burn the sinful body to ashes by means of the *kumbhaka* practice repeated sixty-four times with the syllable "Yaṃ"; then, having reduced the sinful person to ash on the right side by means of the seed-syllable "Yaṃ" repeated thirty-two times, [one should proceed].
11b) Then, by reciting "VAM," one causes a rain of nectar consisting of the letters of the Mātṛkā to fall from the moon upon the forehead;
by bathing the ashes [with this], one gradually saturates the limbs, and by reciting "DHAVA," one makes it firm.

Having produced from the Supreme Self (paramātman) primordial nature (prakṛti), from that the Great Principle (mahat), from that the ego-sense (ahaṃkāra), from that space (ākāśa), from that wind (vāyu), from that fire (tejas), from that water (jala), and from that earth (pṛthivī), and having established each in its own respective place,
[one should worship] the Supreme Self at the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra) with the mantra "So 'haṃ" (I am That).
Having brought the individual soul (jīvātman), shaped like the flame of a lamp, through the door of Kuṇḍalinī to the heart-lotus,

and having established Kuṇḍalinī in the Mūlādhāra, one should contemplate one's own body as being devoid of all impurities and fit for the propitiation of the deity; this is Bhūtaśuddhi (the purification of the elements).
Thus it is said in the Kumārīkalpa:
"Having performed the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) in this manner, one should contemplate oneself in the form of the Goddess.
Then one should perform the deposition of the vital breath (jīvanyāsa), contemplating oneself as the Goddess."
The meaning is that one should contemplate [this]. Then, having meditated upon the goddess as one's own form and placed the hand at the heart, [one recites]:
*āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ haṃ saḥ*.

The vital breaths (*prāṇa*) of Dakṣiṇakālikā are here; *āṃ hrīṃ krāṃ haṃsaḥ*. The life-force (*jīva*) of Dakṣiṇakālikā is stationed here; *āṃ hrīṃ krāṃ haṃsaḥ*. All the sense organs (*sarvendriya*) of Dakṣiṇakālikā are here; *āṃ hrīṃ krāṃ haṃsaḥ*. The speech, mind, and eyes of Dakṣiṇakālikā are here; *āṃ hrīṃ krāṃ haṃsaḥ*.

Having performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (consecration of the vital breaths) with the mantra: "O ear, life-breath, and vital breaths, come here! O mouth, stay for a long time! Svāhā!", and having performed sixteen recitations of the *praṇava* (OM) for the accomplishment of the sixteen purificatory rites (*saṃskāras*), one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the seers (*ṛṣis*) and other elements.

For this vidyā, Bhairava is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chanda), the venerable Dakṣiṇākālīkā is the deity (devatā), Hrīṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Ha is the power (śakti), Krīṃ is the pin (kīlaka); its application (viniyoga) is in recitation for the sake of attaining one’s desired goal.

Having spoken thus with palms joined in reverence (*kṛtāñjali*), one should perform the assignment (*nyāsa*): "Obeisance to the sage Bhairava" on the head; "Obeisance to the *uṣṇik* meter" on the mouth; "Obeisance to the deity Śrī Dakṣiṇakālikā" on the heart; "Obeisance to the seed-syllable *hrīṃ*" on the private parts;
"Obeisance to the power (*śakti*) *huṃ*" on the feet; and "Obeisance to the wedge (*kīlaka*) *krīṃ*" on all limbs. This is done by assigning each part individually.
"māse" refers to the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the ṛṣi and other [constituent elements]. ||12||

12b) As for the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*), it is performed with one's own seed-syllable preceded by the *praṇava* and joined with the six long vowels, or else with the root-mantra repeated twice. This has been stated in the *Svatantra*:

One should perform the placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) using the seed-syllable *praṇava* (oṃ), the syllable *vaṣaṭ*, and the long vowels combined with the earth-mantras (*medināṃ*), as well as the root mantra with the three *khaḍa*s; this is the specific distinction in the *Bhairavī Tantra*. The practitioner of mantras (*mantrī*) should place the six limbs either three times or once according to the sequence. Having thus performed the placement according to the rules, one should then carry out the placement of the letters (*varṇanyāsa*).

Oṃ krāṃ, salutation to both thumbs. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to both index fingers. Oṃ krūṃ, salutation to both middle fingers. Oṃ kraiṃ, salutation to both ring fingers. Oṃ krauṃ, salutation to both little fingers. Oṃ kraḥ, salutation to both palms and backs of the hands. Oṃ krāṃ...

"Hṛdayāya namaḥ" (Salutation to the heart): with the index, middle, and ring fingers, [place it] on the heart. "Oṃ krīṃ śirase svāhā" (Oṃ krīṃ, svāhā to the head): with the index and middle fingers, [place it] on the head. "Oṃ krūṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ" (Oṃ krūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock): having formed a fist, [place it] with the thumb facing downward. "Oṃ kraiṃ kavacāya" (Oṃ kraiṃ, to the armor): [place it] on the back with the fingers of both hands.
For the armor: *Oṃ krauṃ* to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*; [performing this] with the index, middle, and ring fingers upon the three eyes.
With the mantra *Oṃ kraḥ* to the weapon, *phaṭ*, one should strike the triple-clap (*tālatraya*) by snapping the index and middle fingers upward toward the head.

13a) With the mantra *oṃ kraḥ astrāya phaṭ*, one should perform the binding of the directions (*digbandha*) by snapping the fingers with the ring finger and thumb joined in the form of a weapon, [aiming] at the cardinal points, the intermediate directions, and above; then, one should perform the ritual placement of the syllables (*varṇanyāsa*). As follows:
Aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ, *namaḥ* to the heart;
aiṃ aiṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ, *namaḥ* to the right arm; caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ, *namaḥ* to the left arm.

*Paṃ phaṃ vaṃ bhaṃ namaḥ* on the right side; *maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ* on the right arm and the left foot. In all cases, the placement (*nyāsa*) is performed with both thumbs. Then, with the root mantra, perform the mental recitation (*japa*) once, from the feet to the head, and from the head to the feet.

Having performed the placement [of the breath], one should perform the Mātṛkā-nyāsa. As it is stated in the Bhairavī Tantra: "Then one should perform the Varṇa-nyāsa, which bestows divine state and fruit. One should place the letters of the alphabet along with the Bindus on the heart, the two arms, and the pair of feet. Afterwards, one should perform the Vyāpaka-nyāsa for each letter together with the Bindu, extending over the eight limbs and the body as a whole. One should then perform the pervasive placement (vyāpaka) with both hands."
Reciting it in the root-vidyā, one should place the feet first and the head last, and the head first and the feet last; as it is said elsewhere: "First the placement of the Mātṛkās, and then...

Regarding the term "known as Śrīkaṇṭha": according to the opinion of some, one should first perform the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*), the installation of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*), and the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the *mātṛkā* letters, and then assign the seer (*ṛṣi*) and other components. For this *mātṛkā-mantra*, Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandaḥ*), Mātṛkā Sarasvatī is the deity (*devatā*), the consonants are the seed-syllables (*vīja*), and the vowels are the power (*śakti*).

The Śaktis; the Unmanifest (Avyakta) is the Kīlaka; the application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of destroying sins. Alternatively, the application in the ritual placement (nyāsa) is as the mantra of Kālikā. Having thus formed a hollowed cup with the hands, one should perform the placement: "Salutation to Brahmā, the Seer (ṛṣi), on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the metre (chaṃdas), on the mouth; salutation to Mātṛkā, the deity (devatā)."

*Hṛdaye*: Salutation to the seed-syllables *ha-la* at the heart. *Guhye*: Salutation to the powers of the vowels (*svara-śakti*) at the secret place. *Pādayoḥ*: Salutation to the unmanifest (*avyakta*) at the feet. *Sarvāṅge*: Salutation to the *kīlaka* at all limbs. Thus ends the [assignment of] Seer and so forth (*ṛṣyādi*). Now, the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*): *Aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ*: Salutation to both thumbs. *Iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ī*: [Salutation] to both index fingers.
Svāhā! Um ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ um, to the two middle fingers, Vaṣaṭ! Eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ, to the two ring fingers, Huṃ! Oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ oṃ, to the two little fingers, Vauṣaṭ!

14a) Aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ aḥ phaṭ with both palms and backs of the hands. One should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) upon the heart and other parts using these very mantras. The mudrās are as previously stated; [now for] the visualization (*dhyāna*).
One should meditate upon the Goddess of Sacrifice (Yāgadevī), who possesses the splendor of the full moon, is composed entirely of love, has three eyes with flickering red pupils,

and is adorned with white ornaments; she is endowed with a mass of matted hair as fierce as the moon, is serene, holds a book, a rosary, a full pitcher, and a boon-granting gesture in her hands, and stands upon a white lotus.

The lord of practitioners should meditate upon her as measured by the face, the eight [breasts], and the navel. Having thus meditated and worshipped her mentally, he should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*).

As it has been said: "Oṃ ending with 'namaḥ', or else preceded by the *māyā* and *lakṣmī* seeds, either with the *vindu* or devoid of the *vindu*, is declared by the wise to be that which is to be placed. Aṃ namaḥ on the forehead; anāyā..."

*Madhyamāsyāṃ*: *Ā namaḥ* at the round face, moving clockwise with the index, middle, and ring fingers. *Ī namaḥ*, *Īṃ namaḥ* on the right and left eyes with the index and ring fingers; in all cases, the sequence begins from the right. *U namaḥ* on the two ears with the thumbs. *Aṃ namaḥ*.
14b) Ṛ *namaḥ*. With the little finger and thumb on the right and left nostrils: *Ḷ* *namaḥ*, *Ḹ* *namaḥ*. With the middle finger on the right and left cheeks: *E* *namaḥ*, *Ai* *namaḥ*.
With the middle finger, [say] *au namaḥ* on the upper lip and *au namaḥ* on the lower lip;
with the ring finger, *aṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; with both the ring and middle fingers, *a namaḥ* on the face;
and with the little finger, the ring finger, and the middle finger, [say] *aḥ namaḥ* on the navel—at these twenty-three locations.

One should place [the syllables]: *kaṃ* *namaḥ* at the right shoulder; *khaṃ* *namaḥ* at the right elbow; *gaṃ* *namaḥ* at the right wrist; *ghaṃ* *namaḥ* at the base of the fingers of the right hand; *ṅaṃ* *namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers of the right hand;
*chaṃ* at the left shoulder; *jaṃ* *namaḥ* at the left elbow; *jhaṃ* *namaḥ* at the left wrist.
*Na* (namas) at the base of the fingers of the left arm; *haṃ* (namas) at the tips of the fingers of the left hand;

*oṃ* (namas) at the base of the right foot; *ṭa* (namas) at the base of the left foot; *ṭaṃ* (namas) at the ankle of the right foot; *ṇaṃ* (namas) at the base of the toes of the right foot; *ta* (namas) at the tips of the toes of the right foot.
At the base of the left foot: *tha* namaḥ. At the left knee: *daṃ* namaḥ. At the left toes: *dhaṃ* namaḥ. At the base of the left toes: *naṃ* namaḥ. (15a)

*Namaḥ* at the tip of the left toe; *phaṃ namaḥ* on the right side; *vaṃ namaḥ* on the left side; *bhaṃ namaḥ* on the back; *maṃ namaḥ* at the navel; with the little finger, middle finger, and thumb, *maṃ namaḥ* in the abdomen;
with the little finger, middle finger, index finger, and thumb, [place them] at the ten locations starting from the front using the palms.

One should perform the placement (*nyāsa*): *Yaṃ*—salutation to the self of bone, at the heart. *Raṃ*—salutation to the self of blood, on the right shoulder. *Laṃ*—salutation to the self of flesh, on the nape of the neck. *Vaṃ*—salutation to the self of fat, on the left shoulder. *Śaṃ*—salutation to the self of marrow, in the heart.
*Tāṃ*—salutation to the self of semen, from the tip of the right hand to the heart. *Paṃ*—salutation to the self of skin, [at the heart].

From the heart to the tip of the left foot: *Taṃ*—*saṃ* salutation to the Self of semen (*śukrātman*). From the heart to the tip of the right foot: *Haṃ*—*prāṇātmane namaḥ*. From the heart to the tip of the left foot: *Laṃ*—*jīvātmane namaḥ*. From the heart to the abdomen: *Kṣaṃ*—*paramātmane namaḥ*. From the heart to the mouth: [Yaṃ].

Having placed it with the palm of the hand, one should perform the Śrīkaṇṭha-mātṛkā-nyāsa. Then, for the Śrīkaṇṭha-mātṛkā: "Obeisance to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the Seer (Ṛṣi), on the head; obeisance to Gāyatrī, the Metre (Chandas), on the mouth;

15b) Homage to the vowels at the feet. Having formed a hollowed cup with the hands and approached the venerable Dakṣiṇakālikā, this is the application (viniyoga) for the placement upon the body.

Now, the six-limbed [rite]: *inā* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*, and so forth for the index fingers and the others; *hmāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*, and so forth, with *hmīṃ hmūṃ hmauṃ hmauṃ hmaḥ*. Then follows the meditation (*dhyāna*).
[He] who possesses arms like staffs holding a garland of Ruru deer, a noose, a goad,

Having meditated on the weapons as being in the right hand—[the sword] at the top, and so forth—and the rosary in the other, the left;

having mentally worshipped them, one should install Śrīkaṇṭha and the others in those very positions with these same mudrās. [The mudrā] consists of the ring finger and the thumb. As it has been said:
In the *Dakṣiṇāmūrtisaṃhitā*, it is stated: "With flowers, with the ring finger, with the breath, or with the mind, one [worships] another form;

with flowers upon one's own body, using the ring finger together with the thumb; or by means of the mind alone in the locations beginning with the *mūlādhāra*, since the touch of the hand is possible there."

16a) "The placement [of mantras] with the thumbs upon both nostrils is applicable everywhere," according to the statement of the *Ghargharavāhinī*. However, within that [tradition], it says: "One should place [the mantras] with the thumbs and ring fingers"; this refers to the placement of the seers (*ṛṣi*) and so forth, as well as the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) placement on the hands.

This arrangement should be understood as distinct [from the previous one], because all the fingers beginning with the thumb are not prescribed there and because they are presented separately, according to the tradition. The ritual application (*prayoga*) is as follows: *Hmauḥ Aṃ*, salutation to Śrīkaṇṭheśa and Pūrṇodarī at the hairline; *Hmauḥ Āṃ*, [salutation] to Ananteśa...

Hmauṃ Āṃ: To Virata and Mukhavṛti—at the mouth. Hmauṃ Iṃ: To Sthūleśa and Śālmalī—at the right eye. Hmauṃ Īṃ: To Trimūli and Salolākṣī—at the left eye. Hmauṃ Uṃ: To Amareśa and Vartulākṣī—at the right ear. Hmauṃ Ūṃ: To Arghaśada and Dīrghaghoṇā—at the left ear. Hmauṃ Ṛṃ...
*Hmauḥ Ṛṃ*, salutation to *Kṣa* and *Dīrghamukhī* in the right nostril;
*Hmauṃ Ḷṃ*, salutation to *Sthārāva* and *Śa* and *Dīrghajihvā* in the left nostril; *Hmauṃ Ḷṃ*, salutation to *Hṛdeśa* and *Kuṇḍodarī* in the right cheek.
Vyāmagaṇḍe: Hmauṃ Eṃ! To the two with upright hair and upturned lips, Hmauḥ! To the two with disheveled hair and distorted faces, [place] on the lower lip: Hmauḥ!

Oṃ, to Sadyojāteśa and Jvālāmukhī, on the upper row of teeth: Hmauḥ. Oṃ Aḥ, to Mahāseneśa and Vidyāmukhī, on the tongue: Hmauḥ. Kaṃ, to Krodhīśa and Mahākālī, at the base of the right arm: Hmauḥ. Svaṃ, to Caṇḍeśa and Sarasvatī...
At the right elbow: *Hsauḥ Gaṃ* to Gandheśa and Sarvasiddhi-Gaurī;
at the right wrist: *Hmauḥ Dyaṃ* to Śivottama and Trailokyavidyā;
at the base of the fingers of the right hand: *Hmauḥ Eka* to Ekarudra and Maṃtraśakti. At the tips of the fingers of the right hand: [the same].

HMAUḤ CA—Kūrmeśa and Ātmaśakti at the base of the left upper arm; CHHAṂ—Ekanetreśa and Mūrtimatī at the left elbow; HMAUḤ JA—Caturānaneśa and Lambodarī at the left wrist; HMAUḤ UṂ—Akuśeśa and Drāviṇī at the base of the fingers of the left hand.

HMAUḤ AṂ: To Sarveśa and Nāgarī, on the fingers of the left hand. HMAUḤ ṬAṂ SE: To Meṣa and Khecarī, at the base of the right [hand]. HMAUṂ CHAṂ LĀṂ: To Lāṅgalīśa and Mañjarī, on the right knee. (17a)

HMAUḤ UṂ, salutation to Dārukeśarūpī and [Her consort] at the right ankle; HMAUḤ ṬAṂ, salutation to Ardhanārīśvarī and Raṇī at the base of the toes of the right foot; HMAUḤ ṆAṂ, salutation to Umākānteśa and Kākodarī at the base of the toes of the right foot; HMAIḤ TAṂ...
Hmauḥ! Salutation to Āṣāḍhīśa and Pūtanā on the left ankle; hmauḥ!

Salutation to Mīneśa and Śaṅkhinī at the base of the toes of the left foot; hmauḥ! Salutation to Meṣeśa and Arjinī at the tips of the toes of the left foot; hmauḥ! Salutation to Palalohita and Śakāpardinī during the nights.
*Hmauḥ*, to Phaśisvīśa and Kujvīnī on the right side;
*hmauḥ*, to Chagalaṇḍeśa and Kapardinī on the left side; *hmauḥ*, to Maṇḍiraṇḍeśa and Vajrā at the back;
*hmauḥ maṃ*, to Mahākāleśa and Jayā, salutations to the belly; *hmau paṃ*, to the Panvagātman.

In the heart: *Hmauḥ Raṃ* to Valīśa and Mukhī, who are of the nature of blood; to Bhujaṅgeśa and Revatī, at the petal-shoulder (*dalāṃsa*). *Hmau Laṃ* to Pinākīśa and Mādhavī, who are of the nature of flesh; to Khaḍgīśa and Vāruṇī, at the petal-shoulder. *Hmauḥ Vaṃ* [to those] who are of the nature of fat.

17b) *Vāmāsauḥ* *Hmauḥ* *Śam*—to the two selves of the left arm, from the heart onwards; *Vakeśa* *Vāyavyā*—to the right arm, ending with that [heart]; *Hmauḥ* *Ṣam*—to the two selves of impurity (*malātman*), from the heart onwards, to the two arms of Śyeteśa and Vadhāriṇī.
Hmauḥ: to the left arm, to Saṃśukra and Ātmā, to Bhṛgu and Īśa, and to Sahajā; from the heart onwards to the right foot, Vaṃ. Hmauḥ Ha: to Prāṇa and Ātmā, to Lakulīśa and Lakṣmī;
from the heart onwards to the left foot, Hmauḥ Laṃ: to Śakti and Ātmā, to Śiveśa.

With *vyāpinībhyām* and *hmauḥ*, from the heart to the abdomen; with *hmauḥ kṣaṃ* and *krodhātmabhyām saṃvartakeśa-mahāmāyābhyām namaḥ*, from the heart to the mouth. Thus are the Śrīkaṇṭha Mātṛkās. Now, the Ṣoḍhānyāsa according to the Suviratatra.
Having performed the placement (nyāsa) of the pure Mātṛkā,
the practitioner, exerting himself, should place the Mātṛkā ending with the letter *rasa* (the sixteenth vowel), and the syllable *Tāra* (Om) encased within the Mātṛkā.
Thus, one should place the syllable *tāra* (oṃ) enclosed by the word *kāma*, and the word *kāma* enclosed by *tāra*;
the syllable *tāra* enclosed by the two *śaktis*, and the *śakti* enclosed by that [syllable]. One should install [the seed-syllables] as follows: *hāṃ jñāṃ kraṃ kau klaṃ*.
In this manner, the mantra is enclosed by those [terms], and likewise, the mantra is again enclosed by each of those respective [terms].
One should place [it] below.
18a) Having arranged the mantra alone in its natural order (anuloma), one should recite it one hundred and eight times while remaining established in the Mātṛkā.
Thus, the sixteen limbs of Durgā have been proclaimed by Gupta;
likewise those of Tārā, Kālikā, Unmukhī, and Parā.
When this excellent *yāsa* (transposition) has been performed, all sin is destroyed; one should observe the root [mantra] according to the yoga, as follows:

there, as before, for the sake of measurement, there should be the *mātṛkā* and the *mātṛkā*; thus is one [part]. Then, in those very places, with those [syllables], by means of the *mudrā* and the eye, then by the *mudrā*: *Śrīṃ Aṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ*.

*Śrīṃ aṃ* namaḥ on the forehead; *śrīṃ āṃ śrīṃ āṃ śrīṃ āṃ* namaḥ on the two eyebrows. In this sequence, one should assign [the syllables] up to *kṣāṃ*; this is the second [method]. In the same way: *klīṃ śrīṃ klāṃ śrīṃ klāṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*.
"From the face-veil," and so forth; one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) starting from the heart and ending with the mouth using *śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ namaḥ*.
This is the third [method]. *Hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* on the forehead.

*Hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*. On the face. *Hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*. On the right eye, and so forth; *hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* on the heart and so forth, ending with the mouth—this is the fourth [placement]. At the root: *Hāṃ hrīṃ ṛṃ ṛ kla mūlaṃ laṃ hrīṃ*.
*Hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ klaṃ na mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ klaṃ namaḥ* on the forehead.
*Mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ klaṃ mūlaṃ hrīṃ hāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ klaṃ namaḥ* on the forehead. *Mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ klaṃ mūlaṃ hrīṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ klaṃ*.

The fifth [method] is as follows: one should place the root mantra *mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ kraṃ kṝṃ klaṃ namaḥ* on the face-circle (*mukhavṛtti*) and so forth, according to the locations of the Mātṛkās. Then: *krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ hraṃ hraṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dakṣiṇe kālike krīṃ krīṃ hraṃ hraṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ svāhā hāsvā hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ*.

"HŪṂ KRĪṂ KRĪṂ KRĪṂ KALIKAṆEKṢIDA HRĪṂ HRĪṂ HŪṂ KṚṂ KRĪṂ KRĪṂ KRĪṂ NAMAḤ" on the forehead; having thus performed the placement (nyāsa) in sequence upon the locations of the Mātṛkās, one should perform the pervasive placement (vyāpaka) with the root mantra up to the one hundred and eight [syllables]. This is the sixth [section]. Here, the mantra is to be worshipped in the place of the twenty-two constellations (nakṣatras).
The oral tradition. Thus ends the sixfold placement (ṣoḍhānyāsa).
19a) Now, regarding the second sixfold deposition (*ṣoḍhānyāsa*) according to the Karuṭyāmala,
the Lord said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim this secret Ṣoḍhā, O beloved;
this must not be disclosed anywhere if one desires one's own welfare.

O Pārvatī, one should place the camphor (the letter *ka*) enclosed within the letters of the Mātṛkā at the time it resides in the Mothers; indeed, one should install those very letters enclosed within the letters right here.

O Goddess, one should first place the two *kūrca* seeds for the Goddess, then the *savya* and *vaya*, and likewise the *śakti* seed; O Goddess, one should then perform the placement of the root mantra at the beginning.
On the right, one should place the three previous seed-syllables beginning with Kālikā;
then two Kūrca seed-syllables, O Goddess, and again two Lajjā seed-syllables.
O Goddess, when the three [syllables] are thus arranged and joined with the fire-born (Ra), that becomes the *tūryakala* of this [mantra],
O Goddess, by virtue of its pervasiveness.
The sixfold placement (ṣoḍhānyāsa) of the mantra has been taught here in thirty-two sections.
The detailed procedure for this placement has not been written out here for fear of excessive prolixity. The ritual application (*prayoga*) is as follows:
*Oṃ krīṃ krīṃ krāṃ aṃ krīṃ krīṃ aṃ krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ na mama* [on] the forehead (*lalāṭe*). *Āṃ*.
*krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ āṃ krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ āṃ krīṃ krīṃ namaḥ*.
[This is for] the face-enclosure (*mukhavṛti*), and so forth. *kṣaṃ krīṃ krīṃ kṣaṃ krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ kṣaṃ krīṃ krīṃ*.
*Krāṃ* *namaḥ*. One should assign [the mantra] from the heart to the mouth; this is the first [method].
*Aṃ hraṃ hraṃ aṃ hraṃ hraṃ aiṃ hraṃ hraṃ namaḥ*. [Assigning] to the forehead and so forth.
*Kṣaṃ hraṃ hraṃ kṣaṃ hrūṃ hrūṃ hraṃ namaḥ*. From the heart to the mouth; this is the second [method].

*Aṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ aṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ aṃ hrīṃ hrāṃ namaḥ* | On the forehead, and so forth. *Kṣaṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ kṣaṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ kṣaṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ namaḥ*. One should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) starting from the heart and ending at the mouth in the locations of the Mātṛkās; this is the third [method]. *Aṃ dakṣiṇe kālike aṃ dakṣiṇe kālike aṃ*.

"Oṃ, salutation to Dakṣiṇakālikā on the forehead," and so forth; in the locations of the Mātṛkās, one should perform the placement from the heart to the mouth as follows: "kṣaṃ Dakṣiṇakālike, kṣaṃ Dakṣiṇakālike, kṣaṃ Dakṣiṇakālike, salutation"—this is the fourth [method]. Then: "Aṃ krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ, Aṃ hrīṃ krīṃ krīṃ, Aṃ krīṃ krīṃ krāṃ."
"Namaḥ" and so forth; one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) in the locations of the *mātṛkā*. This is the fifth [section].
"Aṃ huṃ hūṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ svāhāṃ, aṃ huṃ hrīṃ svāhāṃ, aṃ hraṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ svāhā namaḥ. [This is] on the forehead and so forth, in the locations of the *mātṛkā*. "Kṣaṃ hraṃ hraṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ."
20a) *svāhā kṣaṃ hraṃ hraṃ hrīṃ svāhā kṣaṃ hraṃ hraṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ svāhā namaḥ*. One should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) from the heart to the face; this is the sixth [section].

Having thus performed the sixfold placement (*ṣoḍhānyāsa*), one should perform the placement of the principles (*tattvanyāsa*). As it is said in the *Svacchanda Tantra*: "One should perform the placement of the principles with the principles of Self, Knowledge, and Śiva.
In the *Kumārikā Tantra*, there is the placement of the seed-syllables (*bījanyāsa*).
One should place all seven seed-syllables of the Cow (Go) in the aperture of Brahma, in the middle of Śiva, on the forehead, in the region of the navel, in the private parts, and in the mouth.
The placement of phonemes (*varṇanyāsa*) according to the *Vīrabhadra Tantra*:
[One should place them] on the head, the two eyes, the forehead, the pair of eyebrows, the ears, the cheeks, the nose, the teeth, the tongue, the region of the shoulders, and the throat.
One should place the mantra-syllables on the arms, heart, sides, back, navel, and in Rudra [the penis], as well as on the hips, anus, hands, and feet;
thus, in Rudra, there is a specific distinction throughout the entire body. In Rudra, one should apply the three powers (tri-śakti) to the penis, hips, anus, hands, and feet.
Everywhere [are] the mantra-syllables;

in the Rudra-liṅga, there is a distinction throughout the entire body. In the *Triśaktiratna*, it is said: "Likewise, [they are located] on the forehead, the two cheeks, the two eyes, and the two ears."
In the pair of nostrils, at the root of the two lower lips,
in the two rows of teeth, between the eyebrows, in the heart, and in the secret region.
One should place [the mantras] upon both arms, both feet, and all the limbs;
in the rite of ritual placement (nyāsa), it should be understood that the sequence begins from the left.
O Dear One, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpakanyāsa*) with the root mantra according to the independent *Bhairavatantra*.
One should perform the exercise fivefold, ninefold, or likewise sevenfold according to the root mantra. The specific application is as follows:
*hrīṃ krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ hraṃ hraṃ hraṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ ātmatattvāya namaḥ* [from the feet upwards].
To the navel, ending at the right [side], O Kālikā, [I offer] obeisance to the Vidyā-tattva. From the left side up to the heart, [I offer] "Māṃ.

*Krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ hraṃ hraṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ svāhā*, obeisance to Śikhāvalā. From the heart up to the head, [I offer] "Hṛkṣadi. Thus is the placement of the principles (*tattva-nyāsa*); here one should perform it with both hands using all the fingers. Now...

The Seed-Syllable Placement (Bījanyāsa): *Krīṃ* namaḥ to the *brahmarandhra*; *krīṃ* namaḥ between the eyebrows; *krīṃ* namaḥ to the forehead; *hraṃ* namaḥ to the navel; *hraṃ* namaḥ to the secret place; *hrīṃ* namaḥ to the mouth; *hrīṃ* namaḥ to all the limbs.
21a) Thus ends the placement of the seed-syllables (*bījanyāsa*). Now follows the placement of the syllables (*avarṇanyāsa*): *krīṃ namaḥ* on the head; *krīṃ namaḥ* on the two eyes.

*Krīṃ* on the forehead; *hūṃ namaḥ hrūṃ* on the two eyes; *hraṃ namaḥ* on the two ears; *hrīṃ namaḥ* on the two cheeks; *hrīṃ namaḥ* on the face; *daṃ namaḥ* on the two rows of teeth; *kṣiṃ namaḥ* on the tongue;
